sentences.zh: 热巧克力机出了一些技术故障，我不得不调试它。

sentences.en: Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·帕伦特。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 17, recorded on March 18th, 2021.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 17 期，录制于 2021 年 3 月 18 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we are super excited to bring you a conversation with our first guest, Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天我和我的联合主持人 Bryce 非常激动能为大家带来与我们首位嘉宾 Sean Parent 的对话。

sentences.en: How is it going, ADSP listeners?
sentences.zh: ADSP 的听众们，你们好吗？

sentences.en: It is just Connor recording a introduction slash prologue before we hop into the conversation with Sean.
sentences.zh: 现在由我 Connor 来录制一段开场白，也就是在进入与 Sean 的对话之前的序言。

sentences.en: Sean Parent, as many of you know, is a senior principal scientist working for Adobe.
sentences.zh: 正如许多人所知，Sean Parent 是 Adobe 的高级首席科学家。

sentences.en: He's been at Adobe since 1993, with the exception of a year in 2009 slash 2010 where he worked for Google, which is where the infamous That's a Rotate story comes from.
sentences.zh: 他自 1993 年起就在 Adobe 工作，除了 2009 到 2010 年间在 Google 工作的那一年，也就是那个臭名昭著的“那是旋转（That's a Rotate）”故事的来源。

sentences.en: Before Adobe, he worked at Apple for roughly five years, and before Apple, he started his career at a company called Orange Micro.
sentences.zh: 在加入 Adobe 之前，他在 Apple 工作了大约五年，而在 Apple 之前，他的职业生涯始于一家名为 Orange Micro 的公司。

sentences.en: That's all I'll say about Sean's work history, as I'm sure you'll hear a lot more about it from him, as he will be a recurring guest on ADSP, the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 关于 Sean 的工作经历我就说这么多，我相信你们会从他本人那里听到更多，因为他将成为 ADSP 播客的常驻嘉宾。

sentences.en: The one thing I do want to add, though, is that if you haven't seen any of Sean's talks, I can't recommend them highly enough.
sentences.zh: 不过，我确实想补充一点，如果你还没看过 Sean 的任何演讲，我强烈推荐你去看看。

sentences.en: My two favorites are C++ Seasoning from 2013 and Generic Programming from 2018.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的两个是 2013 年的《C++ Seasoning》和 2018 年的《Generic Programming》。

sentences.en: Listening to Sean talk is inspiring, and a part of the reason that I gave my first conference talk in 2019,
sentences.zh: 听 Sean 演讲非常鼓舞人心，这也是我 2019 年进行第一次会议演讲的部分原因，

sentences.en: algorithm intuition is because of watching Sean Parent's C++ Seasoning from 2013.
sentences.zh: 关于算法直觉的内容，正是因为观看了 Sean Parent 2013 年的《C++ Seasoning》。

sentences.en: So at this point, I'm going to splice in a quote from his Generic Programming talk in 2018,
sentences.zh: 所以现在，我打算插入一段他 2018 年《Generic Programming》演讲中的引言，

sentences.en: because I think it's absolutely fantastic, and after that, we will hop into our conversation.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得那段话棒极了，在那之后，我们就会进入正题。

sentences.en: Super excited to bring you this conversation with Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 非常激动能为大家带来这次与 Sean Parent 的对话。

sentences.en: And Alex has this beautiful little solution in there for StableSort that builds it up out of all the other algorithMs.
sentences.zh: Alex 在那里为 StableSort 提供了一个非常精妙的小方案，它是用所有其他算法构建出来的。

sentences.en: All the algorithms within the STL fit together like puzzle pieces.
sentences.zh: STL 中的所有算法就像拼图一样完美契合。

sentences.en: I saw this, and I thought, who writes code like this?
sentences.zh: 我看到这个的时候，心想，谁会写出这样的代码？

sentences.en: Okay, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, keep in mind here, I'm working with a bunch of phenomenal engineers, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，请记住，我当时是在和一群杰出的工程师一起工作，对吧？

sentences.en: Great people.
sentences.zh: 都是很棒的人。

sentences.en: These are some of the top people in the industry.
sentences.zh: 他们是业内顶尖的人才。

sentences.en: And I've never seen somebody who writes code like this, okay?
sentences.zh: 但我从未见过有人能写出这样的代码，真的。

sentences.en: This is not like the code that Alex published in his paper five years before, right?
sentences.zh: 这不像 Alex 五年前在论文中发表的代码，对吧？

sentences.en: He's clearly grown and had some time to think about it.
sentences.zh: 他显然成长了，并且花了一些时间去思考。

sentences.en: So it's just this phenomenal piece of work.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一件了不起的作品。

sentences.en: And for me, it was like, I want to write code like that.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，当时的想法就是，我想写出那样的代码。

sentences.en: How do I write code like that?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么写出那样的代码呢？

sentences.en: All right, we are recording our first episode with a gueSt.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们正在录制第一期有嘉宾的节目。

sentences.en: And if you've been listening up till now, you probably have a good idea who it is.
sentences.zh: 如果你一直听到现在，你可能已经猜到是谁了。

sentences.en: The man, the myth, the legend, Sean Parent.
sentences.zh: 那个男人，那个神话，那个传奇，Sean Parent。

sentences.en: How's it going?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Hey, it's going pretty good.
sentences.zh: 嘿，还不错。

sentences.en: So yeah, I've been actually listening to your podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 其实我一直在听你们的播客。

sentences.en: I think I'm current, so I've listened to all of them.
sentences.zh: 我想我已经追平了，所有的节目我都听过了。

sentences.en: It was probably the highlight of my year so far when you tweeted out around Christmas, the photo of you with a glass of eggnog with the caption, and that was a lot of APL.
sentences.zh: 这大概是我今年到目前为止最高光的时刻了，当时你在圣诞节左右发了一条推文，照片里你拿着一杯蛋奶酒，配文是“那真是太多的 APL 了”。

sentences.en: So thank you for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're an easy man to please, I guess.
sentences.zh: 是啊，看来你是个很容易满足的人。

sentences.en: Sean, do you remember the keynote you gave at C++ Now, like 2014?
sentences.zh: Sean，你还记得你在 2014 年 C++ Now 大会上做的主题演讲吗？

sentences.en: It was, you gave a talk where you were talking about getting, I think it was like getting
sentences.zh: 当时你做了一个演讲，谈到了，我想是关于让

sentences.en: Photoshop or something like of that nature running on an iPad.
sentences.zh: Photoshop 或类似的东西在 iPad 上运行。

sentences.en: And what I remember about the talk is there's one point where you're talking about, you know, what's the compute that you have available on the iPad.
sentences.zh: 我对那个演讲的记忆是，有一点你谈到了，你知道，iPad 上可用的计算能力是什么。

sentences.en: And like a small part of it is the serial processing power.
sentences.zh: 其中一小部分是串行处理能力。

sentences.en: And then there's a larger part of it that's the, you know, parallel processing power.
sentences.zh: 然后更大的一部分是，你知道，并行处理能力。

sentences.en: And then you have the GPU.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有 GPU。

sentences.en: And yeah, it was just, I think it's my favorite of your talks.
sentences.zh: 总之，那应该是我最喜欢你的演讲了。

sentences.en: But anyways, I've been thinking about it a lot lately because I now obviously work at NVIDIA and work a lot on parallel computing.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，我最近一直在思考这个问题，因为我现在显然在 NVIDIA 工作，做了很多并行计算方面的工作。

sentences.en: And I just remember, like in hindsight, thinking that talk was really prescient.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，我觉得那个演讲真的很有预见性。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's, I use that slide, that slide's actually from Russell WilliaMs.
sentences.zh: 是的，我用了那张幻灯片，那张幻灯片其实是 Russell Williams 的。

sentences.en: And it's not specific to the iPad.
sentences.zh: 而且它并不局限于 iPad。

sentences.en: It's actually an Intel box that a few years ago he kind of broke down the numbers on.
sentences.zh: 那其实是一台 Intel 机器，几年前他把数据拆解了一下。

sentences.en: But yeah, if you look at where the compute horsepower is in a modern machine, if you're just writing single-threaded code on the, you know, on the CPU with no SIMD,
sentences.zh: 但确实，如果你看看现代机器的计算能力在哪里，如果你只是在 CPU 上写单线程代码，没有 SIMD，

sentences.en: you're using 0.25% of the complete compute capability of the machine.
sentences.zh: 你只使用了机器总计算能力的 0.25%。

sentences.en: You know, most of the MIPS are trapped inside the GPU and increasingly now split between GPU and ML units.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大部分 MIPS 都被困在 GPU 里，现在越来越多地在 GPU 和机器学习单元之间分配。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, one of these days I'm going to, one of these days somebody at NVIDIA is going to teach me something about this machine learning stuff.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，总有一天，NVIDIA 的某个人会教我一些关于机器学习的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely worth looking at.
sentences.zh: 确实值得一看。

sentences.en: I mean, the, you know, my short summary of kind of modern machine learning is, is if you think about, you know, what we write on machines are just functions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对现代机器学习的简短总结是，如果你想想，我们写在机器上的东西只是函数。

sentences.en: And, and we typically come up with some equation for the function.
sentences.zh: 我们通常会为函数想出一些方程。

sentences.en: But any function can be approximated.
sentences.zh: 但任何函数都可以被近似。

sentences.en: And so if you have something where you don't know what the function is, but you can feed enough material to, to a machine learning system,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一些不知道函数是什么的东西，但你可以向机器学习系统提供足够的材料，

sentences.en: it can learn to, to derive an approximate function.
sentences.zh: 它就能学会推导出一个近似函数。

sentences.en: And, and so, you know, that's kind of all, all machine learning is, but, but it does, it does change things.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这就是机器学习的全部，但它确实改变了一些事情。

sentences.en: If you look at an image processing, say, take Lightroom, the, the Lightroom auto button, which, you know, kind of auto adjusts all the sliders.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看图像处理，比如 Lightroom 的“自动”按钮，它会自动调整所有的滑块。

sentences.en: That used to be a very carefully hand-tuned algorithm and trying to look at, well, you know, statistically, how would we want to balance highlights and shadows?
sentences.zh: 那曾经是一个非常精细的手动调优算法，试图去观察，嗯，从统计学上讲，我们想如何平衡高光和阴影？

sentences.en: And what about this kind of image?
sentences.zh: 这种图像该怎么办？

sentences.en: And what about that kind of image?
sentences.zh: 那种图像又该怎么办？

sentences.en: And the approach now is to just get a bunch of experts and have them correct a whole bunch of images and do a really good job and have the machine learn what they do.
sentences.zh: 现在的做法是找一群专家，让他们校正一大堆图像，做得非常出色，然后让机器去学习他们的做法。

sentences.en: And that's the auto button these days.
sentences.zh: 这就是现在的“自动”按钮。

sentences.en: So, so, so you've worked on a, you've worked on Photoshop.
sentences.zh: 所以，你曾在 Photoshop 上工作过。

sentences.en: What are all the things that you've worked on in Adobe?
sentences.zh: 你在 Adobe 还做过哪些工作？

sentences.en: You've worked on Photoshop, Premiere.
sentences.zh: 你做过 Photoshop，Premiere。

sentences.en: Uh, I have not worked on Premiere.
sentences.zh: 呃，我没做过 Premiere。

sentences.en: So at Adobe, um, uh, uh, I started at Adobe working on Photoshop
sentences.zh: 在 Adobe，我最初是在 Photoshop 组工作，

sentences.en: and then we launched, uh, an internet division.
sentences.zh: 然后我们推出了一个互联网部门。

sentences.en: This was way back when Netscape was really hot and, and everybody needed an internet division.
sentences.zh: 那是在 Netscape 非常火的时候，每个人都需要一个互联网部门。

sentences.en: Um, uh, uh, uh, and so I, I ended up working on a shared component about the only surviving piece of that is something called XMP, which is a standard for metadata and how
sentences.zh: 我最终在一个共享组件上工作，其中唯一幸存的部分是名为 XMP 的东西，它是元数据的标准，以及如何

sentences.en: metadata is embedded in documents so that you can, you can pull it out.
sentences.zh: 将元数据嵌入文档中，以便你可以将其提取出来。

sentences.en: Um, uh, uh, from there, I did a stint in Adobe's ATG, which is their advanced technology group or was at the time, uh, a research team.
sentences.zh: 从那里，我在 Adobe 的 ATG 工作了一段时间，也就是他们当时的先进技术组，一个研究团队。

sentences.en: Um, and I was doing, that's where I started research on something called property models,
sentences.zh: 我在那里开始了关于“属性模型”的研究，

sentences.en: which I still, is still something that I continue to work on in my, what little spare time I have.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是我在仅有的业余时间里继续研究的东西。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: uh, uh, while I was in ATG is when Adobe hired and then fired Alex Stepanov and that led to me, uh, and then hired him back and the hiring him back led to me managing him.
sentences.zh: 当我在 ATG 时，Adobe 聘请了 Alex Stepanov，后来又解雇了他，这导致我……然后又把他聘请回来，聘请他回来后我就开始管理他。

sentences.en: Um, and together we formed Adobe software technology lab, which spun out of our research team.
sentences.zh: 我们一起组建了 Adobe 软件技术实验室（ST Lab），它是从我们的研究团队中分拆出来的。

sentences.en: And so I ran Adobe software technology lab for eight years.
sentences.zh: 我管理了 Adobe 软件技术实验室八年。

sentences.en: And, uh, you know, we wrote, wrote the book elements of programming.
sentences.zh: 我们写了《Elements of Programming》这本书。

sentences.en: We created Adobe source libraries.
sentences.zh: 我们创建了 Adobe 源代码库。

sentences.en: We did a whole bunch of stuff internally as part of that effort.
sentences.zh: 作为那项工作的一部分，我们在内部做了很多事情。

sentences.en: And, uh, uh, when ST lab fell apart, uh, I went to Google for a year, worked on Chrome OS,
sentences.zh: 当 ST Lab 解散时，我去了 Google 工作了一年，负责 Chrome OS，

sentences.en: came back to Adobe to work on revel, which was a consumer version of Lightroom for, uh,
sentences.zh: 后来回到 Adobe 负责 Revel，那是 Lightroom 的消费者版本，

sentences.en: uh, we shipped it for iPhone, iPad, and desktop, and it was a precursor for Lightroom mobile.
sentences.zh: 我们为 iPhone、iPad 和桌面端发布了它，它是 Lightroom Mobile 的前身。

sentences.en: It was running the same imaging engine that Lightroom runs.
sentences.zh: 它运行的是与 Lightroom 相同的成像引擎。

sentences.en: And so I pivoted from working on revel, uh, just before revel was canceled, uh, to start
sentences.zh: 所以在 Revel 被取消之前，我从 Revel 的工作转向了

sentences.en: Lightroom mobile.
sentences.zh: Lightroom 移动版。

sentences.en: And so I did Lightroom mobile and then, uh, got the imaging engine going inside the browser.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了 Lightroom Mobile，然后让成像引擎在浏览器中运行起来。

sentences.en: So that was Lightroom web.
sentences.zh: 那就是 Lightroom Web。

sentences.en: And then after doing that, uh, guy named Dave Howell walked into my office one day and said, could we just put Photoshop on the iPad?
sentences.zh: 在那之后，一个叫 Dave Howell 的人有一天走进我的办公室说，我们能不能把 Photoshop 放到 iPad 上？

sentences.en: And I said, I think I know how I would do that.
sentences.zh: 我说，我想我知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: And that launched the effort to put Photoshop on iPad.
sentences.zh: 于是启动了将 Photoshop 移植到 iPad 的工作。

sentences.en: So, uh, did, did Photoshop mobile and, and Photoshop mobile is somewhat of a larger effort.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了 Photoshop Mobile，这是一个规模相当大的工程。

sentences.en: If you can probably read the tea leaves, if you look at, at people were hiring these days, uh,
sentences.zh: 如果你能读懂其中的门道，看看这些天人们在招聘什么，

sentences.en: but part of that was taking, uh, the Photoshop code base and turning it into a library, uh, that contains kind of all the interactive logic.
sentences.zh: 但其中的一部分是将 Photoshop 代码库变成一个库，其中包含了所有的交互逻辑。

sentences.en: So, so you can't just do batch processing with it, but you can attach a UI to this library and, uh, and put Photoshop in other places.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能只用它进行批处理，但你可以为这个库附加一个 UI，把 Photoshop 放到其他地方。

sentences.en: And so recently I've been doing some work putting Photoshop in other places, which haven't shipped yet.
sentences.zh: 所以最近我一直在做一些把 Photoshop 放到其他地方的工作，这些还没发布。

sentences.en: And, uh, and right now I'm putting together a white paper and maybe looking to hire somebody and, uh, uh, get back in, in the research side of things a little bit.
sentences.zh: 现在我正在写一份白皮书，也许打算招聘某人，重新回到研究领域。

sentences.en: I've got an idea for, uh, a potential product that's, uh, a little bit long lead and it's gonna, gonna require a little research to, to feed into it.
sentences.zh: 我有一个潜在产品的想法，周期比较长，需要一些研究来支撑它。

sentences.en: Spicy.
sentences.zh: 够劲。

sentences.en: So when, when you, um, when you, when did you first meet Alex, did you know Stepanov before, uh, you became his manager?
sentences.zh: 那么，你是什么时候第一次见到 Alex 的？在你成为他的经理之前，你认识 Stepanov 吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 认识。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, um, uh, uh, uh, uh, when I was working in Adobe's ATG group, one of my colleagues there,
sentences.zh: 当我在 Adobe 的 ATG 组工作时，我的一位同事，

sentences.en: uh, was, uh, an individual, Larry Massenter and Larry had worked with Alex at Bell Labs years ago and was friends with Alex and Larry invited Alex to give a talk at Adobe.
sentences.zh: Larry Massenter，他多年前在贝尔实验室和 Alex 一起工作过，是 Alex 的朋友，Larry 邀请 Alex 来 Adobe 做演讲。

sentences.en: And at that time, Alex was, uh, vice president at Compaq, uh, computers, if you remember who
sentences.zh: 当时，Alex 是 Compaq 电脑公司的副总裁，如果你还记得他们的话，

sentences.en: they were, they made kind of, you know, portable PC devices and Compaq was getting bought out by HP.
sentences.zh: 他们制造便携式 PC 设备，而 Compaq 当时正被 HP 收购。

sentences.en: And so Alex had been in HP research before, but now he's a VP at Compaq going through a transition to Hewlett Packard.
sentences.zh: Alex 之前在 HP 研究院工作过，但现在他是 Compaq 的副总裁，正在经历向惠普的过渡。

sentences.en: And, uh, so Alex came in and gave a talk on STL and afterwards I went up to him and told him, Hey, I enjoyed the talk and, uh, uh, a fan of your work on STL.
sentences.zh: Alex 过来做了关于 STL 的演讲，之后我走过去告诉他，嘿，我很喜欢这个演讲，我是你 STL 工作的粉丝。

sentences.en: And it was a, you know, wonderful talk.
sentences.zh: 那真是一场精彩的演讲。

sentences.en: And he asked what I did and we started chatting about at the time I was researching property models and he said, you know, that's actually interesting.
sentences.zh: 他问我是做什么的，我们开始聊天，当时我正在研究属性模型，他说，你知道，那很有趣。

sentences.en: So we ended up going up to my office and talking for like four hours and I gave him a demo of property models and we just chatted.
sentences.zh: 于是我们去了我的办公室聊了大约四个小时，我给他演示了属性模型，我们就这样聊开了。

sentences.en: And at some point in that conversation, he said, uh, he said, he said, you know, I've,
sentences.zh: 在谈话的某个时刻，他说，你知道，我

sentences.en: I've really missed being an engineer and doing engineering.
sentences.zh: 真的很怀念做工程师和从事工程工作的感觉。

sentences.en: And I said, well, why don't you go back to it?
sentences.zh: 我说，那你为什么不回去做呢？

sentences.en: Like what's stopping you?
sentences.zh: 是什么阻止了你？

sentences.en: And he just kind of laughed and shrugged it off.
sentences.zh: 他只是笑了笑，耸了耸肩。
